If each value is at most U, the weighted logarithmic sum bounds log ell_z below by −((1−w_z)/w_z)log U, uniformly since w_z≥v. Hence the affine evaluation limit is positive at every base, and therefore positive throughout its convex hull. The frame supplies positive compatible body limits.

overlap.comparison: Uses the same determinant/covariance invariance and the same ell=1 trial and slab constants for unpenalized sampled-concave arrays. Its attainment relies on proper-minor quotas and parity saturation. It does not give the arithmetic-penalty estimate or its no-quota affine formulation.

Proves qualitative vanishing of unit-normal displacements at unpenalized near-minima over positive continuous concave weights, with minor quotas. The present theorem is a penalized affine statement with an explicit rate and proper-own-section bound under only the original compact frame.

Bounds ordinary and buffered maximizing-mark boundary distances in a tied body-dependent profile. The slab and centroid arguments coincide in principle, but its displacement bound comes from that fixed profile, without an optimized affine multiplier or arithmetic penalty.

readability: The final distance estimate is in the mass-one representative frame. The theorem concerns proper shifted traces in their own fibers, and needs no smoothness of supporting traces elsewhere.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The weighted arithmetic penalty yields fixed-scale compactness and the quantitative unit-normal shift bound from the assumed original compact frame. The resulting boundary distance guarantees proper own sections.
